name: Vienna
tagline: Imperial palaces, coffee houses and music in the grand manner
bestMonths: Apr, May, Jun, Jul and Aug
whenBlurb: Late spring and early autumn are mildest; December brings Christmas markets and January-February the glittering ball season, though winter beyond that is grey and cold.

ourTake.lede: Vienna rewards a slower pace than most visitors give it, the pleasure is in the coffee houses, the concert halls and the museums, not in racing between sights. Prioritise a proper opera or Musikverein evening and an afternoon that does nothing but a Kaffeehaus and a walk; skip the tourist-trap Mozart concerts sold on the Kärntner Straße. Time a visit for the ball season in winter or the arts festival in early summer, and don't overlook the outer districts for food and wine.
ourTake.comeIf: You want imperial grandeur, world-class music and museums, and coffee-house afternoons at an unhurried pace.
ourTake.skipIf: You are after beaches, wild landscapes or nightlife-driven energy rather than culture and refinement.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Hotel Sacher Wien
items.area: Innere Stadt (1st), behind the State Opera
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: The definitive Viennese address since 1876, family-owned, opera-facing, and the birthplace of the Sachertorte.

items.name: Rosewood Vienna
items.description: A restored 19th-century palace on Petersplatz where Mozart once lived, Rosewood's polished contemporary hand on the Old Town.

items.name: Park Hyatt Vienna
items.area: Innere Stadt (1st), Am Hof / Goldenes Quartier
items.description: A former bank turned calm, contemporary grand hotel in the luxury-shopping quarter, the spa pool sits in the old vault.

items.name: Hotel Imperial, a Luxury Collection Hotel
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A private palace of 1863 on the Ring, the grande dame that has housed nearly every head of state to visit Vienna.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental, Vienna
items.description: The group's first Austrian house, a former court building reborn with Mandarin Oriental precision and a landmark spa.

items.name: Palais Coburg Residenz
items.description: A suites-only palace with one of the world's great wine cellars, and a two-star kitchen behind its columns.

items.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Vienna
items.description: Four linked 19th-century palaces on the Ring, Ritz-Carlton service behind a historic façade, with the city's best hotel rooftop bar.

items.name: Anantara Palais Hansen Vienna
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A Theophil Hansen palace on the Ring, reborn under Anantara, grand bones, a serious spa, a Michelin kitchen within.

items.name: Hotel Bristol, a Luxury Collection Hotel
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A 1892 landmark facing the opera house, fin-de-siècle antiques, Austrian art, and a quietly grand sense of occasion.

items.name: Almanac Palais Vienna
items.description: Two neo-Baroque palaces across from the Stadtpark, suite-led, art-filled, with an original Klimt on the wall.

items.name: The Amauris Vienna
items.description: A small, discreet Relais & Châteaux townhouse a step from the opera, private, refined, all quiet luxury.

items.name: Hotel Sans Souci Wien
items.description: A design-led house beside the MuseumsQuartier, art on the walls, a fine spa, a younger sense of glamour.

items.name: Grand Hotel Wien
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: One of the four historic grand hotels of the Ring, classical grandeur and a celebrated rooftop dining room.

items.name: Andaz Vienna Am Belvedere
items.description: A Renzo Piano-designed tower by the Belvedere gardens, contemporary, light, with a rooftop pool over the city.

items.name: Le Méridien Vienna
items.description: A design hotel on the Ring between the opera and the Hofburg, contemporary art and an easy, central polish.

items.name: Hotel MOTTO, Vienna
items.description: A theatrical, 1900s-Paris-inspired house with the city's most fashionable rooftop restaurant.

items.name: The Guesthouse Vienna
items.description: A Terence Conran-designed boutique beside the Albertina, warm, residential, beautifully made.

items.name: Hotel Josefine
items.description: A characterful literary-themed townhouse just off the Ring, individual, well-priced, quietly charming.

items.name: Hollmann Beletage Design & Boutique Hotel
items.description: A hidden design guesthouse on the first floor of a historic building, intimate, personal, central.

items.name: Altstadt Vienna
items.description: An art-filled townhouse hotel in the bohemian Spittelberg lanes, every room individually designed.

items.name: Schönbrunn Palace
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Palace and Gardens of Schönbrunn
items.description: The Habsburgs' 1,441-room summer residence, all Rococo gilding and Maria Theresa yellow, with formal parterres climbing to the hilltop Gloriette. A private after-hours or Grand Tour guided visit spares multi-generational groups the queues, and the park's gravel walks are easy for elders and children alike.

items.name: Gloriette and Palace Gardens
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Palace and Gardens of Schönbrunn
items.description: The colonnaded triumphal arch crowning Schönbrunn's hill, built as Maria Theresa's banqueting pavilion, now with a café under its arches and the finest panorama back over the palace and city. The climb through the Baroque gardens is the classic golden-hour walk before dinner.

items.name: Tiergarten Schönbrunn (Vienna Zoo)
credentials: Part of the Schönbrunn UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The world's oldest zoo still in operation, founded in 1752, with giant pandas and giraffes housed inside original Baroque pavilions. A reliable multi-generational win, grandparents and small children both delighted, set within the palace grounds.

items.name: Hofburg Imperial Palace
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of Vienna UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: Six centuries of Habsburg power in one sprawling complex of 18 wings and 19 courtyards, still the working seat of the Austrian president. The Imperial Apartments and Sisi Museum tell the real story of Empress Elisabeth beyond the films.

items.name: Sisi Museum & Imperial Apartments
items.description: Empress Elisabeth's private world inside the Hofburg, her gymnastics equipment, death mask and the reconstructed court silver, laid out through Franz Joseph's living and audience rooms. A tightly curated hour that fascinates teenagers as much as elders.

items.name: Spanish Riding School
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Classical horsemanship of the Spanish Riding School
items.description: The white Lipizzaner stallions performing haute école dressage in Fischer von Erlach's chandelier-lit Winter Riding School, a tradition unbroken since the 18th century. Book the gala performance, or the quieter morning training session with a private box for the family.

items.name: Upper Belvedere
credentials: World's largest collection of Gustav Klimt paintings
Part of the Historic Centre of Vienna UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: Prince Eugene's Baroque summer palace holds the world's largest Klimt collection, including 'The Kiss' in its own gilded room, above formal gardens sweeping down to the Lower Belvedere. The palace terrace offers one of the loveliest framed views of the city skyline.

items.name: Lower Belvedere & Orangery
items.description: The quieter half of the Belvedere estate, Prince Eugene's private state rooms, the Marble Hall and the Hall of Grotesques, used for changing exhibitions. Combine with a stroll through the tiered French garden between the two palaces.

items.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
credentials: World's largest collection of paintings by Pieter Bruegel the Elder
items.description: The Habsburgs' imperial art collection, the world's greatest holding of Bruegel, plus Vermeer, Velázquez, Raphael and Titian, under a domed staircase Klimt himself decorated. The palatial café beneath the cupola is a destination in itself.

items.name: Albertina
credentials: One of the world's largest and most important print rooms
items.description: A former Habsburg residence above the opera holding one of the world's foremost graphic collections, Dürer's 'Young Hare', Monet, Picasso, shown alongside the restored imperial state rooms. Central, compact and elegant, ideal for a focused morning.

items.name: Leopold Museum
credentials: World's largest collection of works by Egon Schiele
items.description: The world's largest Egon Schiele collection alongside Klimt's 'Death and Life' and a definitive survey of Viennese Modernism, in a luminous white cube in the MuseumsQuartier. The clearest single window into Vienna 1900.

items.name: mumok (Museum moderner Kunst)
items.description: Austria's largest museum of modern and contemporary art, Warhol, Picasso, Viennese Actionism, inside a windowless basalt monolith in the MuseumsQuartier. For collectors and design-minded travellers rather than first-timers.

items.name: MAK, Museum of Applied Arts
items.description: Vienna's temple of design and decorative arts, from Wiener Werkstätte silver and Thonet bentwood to Klimt's full-scale Stoclet Frieze cartoons. Essential for anyone furnishing a home or drawn to craft; its garden bar is a stylish evening spot.

items.name: MuseumsQuartier
credentials: Among the largest cultural complexes in the world
items.description: One of the world's largest cultural complexes, Leopold, mumok, the Kunsthalle and Baroque courtyards filled with the signature painted 'Enzi' loungers. A relaxed base to graze between museums, with cafés for those who prefer to sit while others tour.

items.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral (Stephansdom)
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of Vienna UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: Vienna's soaring Gothic heart, its 136-metre south tower the tallest church in Austria and its zigzag tiled roof a city emblem. Climb the 343 steps of the tower, or take the lift to the north tower with elders, and tour the catacombs below.

items.name: Karlskirche (St. Charles's Church)
items.description: Fischer von Erlach's Baroque masterpiece, its green copper dome flanked by two Trajan-style columns, built as a vow after the 1713 plague. A panorama lift rises into the cupola for a close look at the frescoes, a rare vantage that thrills all ages.

items.name: Peterskirche (St. Peter's Church)
items.description: A jewel-box Baroque oval tucked just off the Graben, with a gilded pulpit, trompe-l'oeil dome and free lunchtime organ recitals. A quiet, discreet pause in the middle of the shopping streets.

items.name: Vienna State Opera (Staatsoper)
credentials: One of the world's foremost opera houses
items.description: One of the world's leading opera houses, staging a different work almost every night with an orchestra drawn from the Vienna Philharmonic. Reserve a private box; the guided backstage tour and elegant intermission suppers suit families building an evening together.

items.name: Musikverein (Golden Hall)
credentials: Venue of the annual Vienna New Year's Concert
items.description: The 'Golden Hall', home of the Vienna Philharmonic since 1870 and stage for the televised New Year's Concert, prized for acoustics considered among the finest on earth. A gilt-and-caryatid room where hearing a concert is the whole point of the trip for many.

items.name: Wiener Konzerthaus
items.description: The city's other great hall, a 1913 building with four auditoriums whose programme ranges beyond classical into jazz and world music. The choice for a more adventurous evening, from September through June.

items.name: Haus der Musik
items.description: An interactive sound museum in the former home of the Vienna Philharmonic, where you can 'conduct' a virtual orchestra and explore the physics of music. The rare cultural stop that genuinely absorbs children and grandparents at once.

items.name: Vienna Boys' Choir at the Hofburgkapelle
credentials: Founded 1498, one of the oldest choirs in the world
items.description: The choir founded in 1498 sings Sunday Mass in the Hofburg's Imperial Chapel, an intimate and moving ritual, and performs full concerts at its own MuTh hall. Reserved seats spare families the scramble for the small chapel.

items.name: The Ringstrasse
items.description: The 5.3-km grand boulevard Franz Joseph laid over the old city walls, lined with the Opera, Parliament, City Hall, university and twin museums, the finest ensemble of 19th-century monumental architecture in Europe. Best seen from a private car or the vintage tram that circles it.

items.name: Austrian Parliament Building
items.description: Theophil Hansen's Greek-temple statement of democracy, fronted by the Pallas Athene fountain and newly restored throughout. Guided tours reveal the columned halls; the rooftop terrace and its restaurant offer a fresh angle on the Ring.

items.name: Vienna City Hall (Rathaus) & Rathausplatz
items.description: A soaring neo-Gothic pile whose square hosts the year's great open-air events, the Christmas market, summer film festival and an ice-skating 'Dream on Ice' in winter. A lively family gathering point at every season.

items.name: Stadtpark
items.description: Vienna's first public park along the river Wien, home to the gilded Johann Strauss II monument, the city's most photographed statue. A gentle, central green break with a pond and café, easy for every generation.

items.name: Burggarten & Palm House
items.description: The former imperial private garden behind the Hofburg, with a Mozart monument in flowers and an Art Nouveau glass Palmenhaus sheltering a butterfly house and an elegant café-brasserie. A discreet, sheltered oasis a step from the Ring.

items.name: Volksgarten Rose Garden
items.description: A formal French garden on the Ring with thousands of rose bushes framing the neoclassical Theseus Temple, best in June bloom. A romantic, quiet counterpoint to the grand buildings around it.

items.name: Prater & Wiener Riesenrad
items.description: The great public park with its historic Giant Ferris Wheel of 1897, immortalised in 'The Third Man', turning slowly over the city. Hire a private gondola with dinner service, then let children loose in the funfair and adults walk the leafy central avenue.

items.name: Hundertwasserhaus
items.description: Friedensreich Hundertwasser's riotously colourful 1985 municipal apartment block, with undulating floors, onion domes and trees growing from the windows. A quick, joyful photo stop that breaks up the imperial grandeur, best paired with the museum nearby.

items.name: Kunst Haus Wien, Museum Hundertwasser
items.description: The artist's own museum in a rebuilt Thonet furniture factory, its wavy floors and green façade a full immersion in his ecological, anti-straight-line philosophy. The permanent Hundertwasser collection plus rotating photography shows, with a garden café.

items.name: Naschmarkt
items.description: Vienna's great 1.5-km market of 120-plus stalls, spices, cheeses, olives, and Middle Eastern and Asian produce that make vegetarian and Indian-friendly dining genuinely easy. Graze the mezze and falafel counters; the Saturday flea market is a cult ritual.

items.name: Café Central
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture
items.description: The vaulted, cathedral-like coffeehouse where Trotsky and Freud once sat, now serving Melange and towering pastries under marble columns. Grand and famous, arrive early or reserve to avoid the queue with a group.

items.name: Café Landtmann
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture
items.description: Freud's regular café on the Ring by the Burgtheater, a wood-panelled institution since 1873 with a broad terrace and a proper kitchen for lunch, not just cake. The most comfortable of the grand cafés for a leisurely multi-generational sit.

items.name: Café Sacher & the Original Sachertorte
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture
items.description: The plush café of the Hotel Sacher, home of the original 1832 Sachertorte, served behind the Opera in red-velvet rooms. The definitive Vienna cake ritual; the box of torte travels home well as a gift.

items.name: Demel
items.description: The former imperial court confectioner on the Kohlmarkt, where white-gloved staff serve pastries beneath mirrored salons and you can watch the bakers at work. Old-world theatre and superb sweets, moments from the Hofburg.

items.name: Café Sperl
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture
items.description: A near-untouched 1880 coffeehouse with billiard tables, newspaper racks and worn Thonet chairs, the archetype away from the tourist crush. The place to linger over an Einspänner and read, exactly as the Viennese do.

items.name: The Graben & Kohlmarkt
items.description: The elegant pedestrian spine of the old city, from the Baroque Plague Column down to the luxury houses of the Kohlmarkt, Cartier, Louis Vuitton and the like, ending at the Hofburg gate. Vienna's discreet address for shopping and window-strolling.

items.name: Spittelberg quarter
items.description: A pocket of cobbled Biedermeier lanes behind the MuseumsQuartier, full of small galleries, artisan shops, wine bars and a beloved Advent market. The 7th district at its most walkable and characterful, good for an unhurried afternoon.

items.name: Grinzing & the Heuriger wine taverns
credentials: Viennese Heuriger culture, UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage
items.description: A wine-village on the city's northern edge where growers pour their own Grüner Veltliner in leafy courtyards beside Biedermeier villas. A relaxed, convivial evening of new wine and buffet food; a private car up and back suits a larger party.

items.name: Kahlenberg viewpoint
items.description: The Vienna Woods summit above the vineyards, with a sweeping terrace over the whole city and the Danube, plus a café for a gentle finish. The classic drive-up panorama, no exertion required, dazzling after dark.

items.name: Nussberg vineyard walk
items.description: Terraced vineyards on the city's edge where open-air wine taverns like Wieninger and Sirbu look straight down over Vienna at sunset. A quietly spectacular alternative to Grinzing for a glass with a view.

items.name: Zentralfriedhof (Central Cemetery)
items.description: One of Europe's largest cemeteries, with honorary graves of Beethoven, Brahms, Schubert and the Strauss family clustered near a monumental Art Nouveau church. A surprisingly serene, parkland pilgrimage for music lovers.

items.name: Secession Building & Beethoven Frieze
items.description: The gold-domed 1898 manifesto of the Vienna Secession, 'To every age its art' over the door, sheltering Klimt's monumental Beethoven Frieze in the basement. A compact, essential stop for the Vienna 1900 story.

items.name: Wachau Valley (day trip)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Wachau Cultural Landscape
items.description: A UNESCO-listed stretch of the Danube between Melk and Krems, terraced with apricot orchards and world-class Grüner Veltliner and Riesling vineyards, threaded with river villages. A private car or chartered boat makes for a superb, unhurried day out of the city.

items.name: Melk Abbey
credentials: Within the Wachau UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: A vast ochre Benedictine abbey on a bluff over the Danube, its Baroque library and gilded church among Europe's great interiors. The natural anchor for a Wachau day, ideally reached before the tour coaches.

items.name: Dürnstein
credentials: Within the Wachau UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The blue-and-white Baroque abbey tower and the castle ruin where Richard the Lionheart was held make this the prettiest Wachau village. Walk its single lane, taste at a riverside cellar, then continue down the Danube.

items.name: Bratislava (day trip)
items.description: The Slovak capital, its compact old town crowned by a hilltop castle, reached in 75 minutes by the fast Twin City Liner catamaran along the Danube. An easy second-country outing, carry passports, as it crosses a border.

items.name: Klosterneuburg Monastery
items.description: A grand Augustinian monastery just outside the city, with the priceless enamelled Verdun Altar of 1181, imperial state rooms and one of Austria's oldest wineries in its cellars. A short, rich half-day with a wine tasting to close.

items.name: Schloss Hof
items.description: Prince Eugene's restored country palace on the Marchfeld plain, with terraced Baroque gardens, a working estate farm and animals that charm younger visitors. A calmer, greener imperial day trip than the city palaces.

items.name: Steirereck im Stadtpark
items.description: Heinz and Birgit Reitbauer's temple of modern Austrian cooking, one of only two three-star tables in the country.

items.name: Restaurant Amador
items.description: Juan Amador's avant-garde cooking in the vaulted cellars of a Grinzing winery, Austria's other three-star.

items.name: Silvio Nickol Gourmet Restaurant
items.description: Precise, contemporary cooking behind the columns of Palais Coburg, beside one of the world's great wine cellars.

items.name: Konstantin Filippou
items.description: Greek-Austrian roots and purist modern technique in a dark, elegant room with the kitchen in full view.

items.name: Mraz & Sohn
items.description: Lukas and Markus Mraz's witty, wildly individual cooking, Austria's most talked-about kitchen, and Falstaff's Chef of the Year.

items.name: Restaurant Doubek
items.description: Stefan Doubek won two stars before turning 32, meticulous cooking over four live fires, with quiet Japanese influences.

items.name: TIAN Restaurant Vienna
items.description: Vegetarian fine dining that earned a star on its own terms, refined, seasonal, entirely meat-free.

items.name: JOLA
items.description: A rare starred vegan kitchen, inventive, produce-led cooking that never feels like it's going without.

items.name: Glasswing by Alexandru Simon
items.description: French technique and quiet ambition, one of the city's brightest recent stars, and a Falstaff favourite.

items.name: APRON
items.description: Creative, internationally-inflected tasting menus from a kitchen on a fast rise up the guides.

items.name: Pramerl & the Wolf
items.description: A former corner tavern turned surprise-menu star, casual on the surface, seriously good beneath.

items.name: Restaurant Edvard
items.description: Paul Gamauf's refined, produce-driven cooking inside the Palais Hansen on the Ring.

items.name: Esszimmer
items.description: Modern cooking with Italian and Asian threads, a quietly assured one-star in the Old Town.

items.name: Herzig
items.description: Modern cooking and a deep wine list in a smart room away from the tourist centre.

items.name: aend
items.description: An avant-garde, ingredient-led kitchen with a cult following, precise, minimal, quietly radical.

items.name: Z'SOM
items.description: South American technique meets Central European produce, a fresh, surprising one-star.

items.name: Le Ciel by Toni Mörwald
items.description: Classical fine dining on the Grand Hotel's roof, a long-held favourite for a dressed-up Viennese evening.

items.name: Fabios
items.description: The city's most enduringly fashionable Italian, a see-and-be-seen room off the Graben.

items.name: Zum Schwarzen Kameel
items.description: A 1618 institution of Jugendstil tiles and open sandwiches, Viennese classics where the city has always gathered.

items.name: Skopik & Lohn
items.description: A buzzy, ink-ceilinged neighbourhood restaurant doing modern Viennese cooking with real flair.

items.name: Mochi
items.description: Lively, informal Japanese cooking with modern turns, one of the most-loved everyday tables in the city.

items.name: Meierei im Stadtpark
items.description: Steirereck's relaxed little sister, a legendary goulash and a cheese counter to lose an afternoon to.

items.name: Gasthaus Pöschl
items.description: A tiny, warm tavern doing Austrian home cooking properly, the kind of room Vienna does best.

items.name: Plachutta Wollzeile
items.description: The temple of Tafelspitz, boiled beef in copper pots, carved and served with real ceremony.

items.name: Figlmüller
items.description: Home of the schnitzel that overhangs the plate, a Viennese rite of passage since 1905.

items.name: Griechenbeisl
items.description: Vienna's oldest inn, from 1447, vaulted rooms where Beethoven, Schubert and Mark Twain all signed the wall.

items.name: TIAN Bistro
items.description: TIAN's easy-going bistro, seasonal, regional vegetarian and vegan cooking at an everyday price.

items.name: Café Central
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture (2011)
A landmark of Viennese café history
items.description: The grand literary coffee house of Loos, Trotsky and Freud, vaulted, marble, and gloriously Viennese.

items.name: Café Landtmann
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture (2011)
items.description: Vienna's most sophisticated coffee house since 1873, the Ring café of politicians, writers and families.

items.name: Demel
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture (2011)
items.description: The former imperial court confectioner, founded 1786, part patisserie, part museum, entirely Viennese.

items.name: Café Sperl
credentials: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Viennese Coffee House Culture (2011)
One of Vienna's best-preserved historic cafés
items.description: An 1880 coffee house barely changed in a century, billiard tables, newspapers, and the real, unhurried thing.

items.name: Loos American Bar
credentials: A defining venue of Viennese bar history
items.description: Adolf Loos's 1908 jewel-box in onyx and marble, the first cocktail bar in Vienna, and a landmark of modern design.

items.name: Tür 7
credentials: Falstaff Bar Guide 2025, 96 points, joint No. 1 in Austria
The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: A ring-the-bell speakeasy that tops the national bar rankings, inventive drinks and a warm, in-the-know room.

items.name: Josef Cocktailbar
credentials: Falstaff Bar Guide 2025, 95 points, joint No. 2 in Austria
items.description: A polished modern cocktail bar with a Styrian accent, one of the very best drinks addresses in the city.

items.name: Kleinod
credentials: The World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery
items.description: A backlit Old Town nook that has led Vienna's cocktail revival for a decade, clear, light spirits done beautifully.

items.name: Dino's Apothecary Bar
items.description: An apothecary-themed cocktail bar mixing with precision and theatre, a favourite of the city's drinks crowd.

items.name: Atmosphere Rooftop Bar
credentials: Atop The Ritz-Carlton, a MICHELIN One-Key hotel
items.description: The city's best hotel rooftop, cocktails over the Ringstrasse rooftops, with St Stephen's spire in the distance.

items.name: Das Loft Bar
items.area: Innere Stadt (1st), SO/ Vienna, Danube Canal
credentials: A landmark high-level bar atop the SO/ Vienna hotel
items.description: A glass-walled 18th-floor bar under a vast coloured-glass ceiling, the widest view over the city.

items.name: Barfly's Club
items.description: A legendary, encyclopaedic hotel bar, hundreds of spirits and a bartender who has seen it all.

plan.heading: 4 days in Vienna, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Hofburg and the Spanish Riding School morning exercise, then a mélange at Café Central under its vaults.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: St. Stephen's Cathedral and the Graben, then the Kohlmarkt to Demel for the sachertorte question settled properly.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Steirereck in the Stadtpark, Austria's finest table and among the world's fifty best.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Kunsthistorisches Museum for the Bruegel room and the Vermeer, a whole morning.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Belvedere for Klimt's Kiss in the palace it was made for.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A wine tavern evening at a Grinzing Heuriger, or dinner at Konstantin Filippou in the first district for the two-star kitchen.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Schönbrunn Palace and its gardens up to the Gloriette before the crowds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Secession building for Klimt's Beethoven Frieze, then the Naschmarkt for a long graze.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: The State Opera if the season allows, supper after at the Bristol's Bristol Lounge.

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Coffee houses and the modern city

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Leopold Museum in the MuseumsQuartier for Schiele and Klimt, then coffee at Café Sperl.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Albertina for the graphic collection and the Monet-to-Picasso rooms.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final dinner at Amador, the three-star cellar in the vaults of a Grinzing winery.

items.name: Innere Stadt (1st District)
items.description: The historic core around the cathedral and opera, grand, central, and priced accordingly.

items.name: Neubau (7th District)
items.description: Design shops, small restaurants and the MuseumsQuartier nearby, for a lower-key, creative base.

items.name: Leopoldstadt (2nd District)
items.description: Across the canal by the Prater, increasingly good for food and a little more local.

events.name: Vienna Opera Ball
events.note: The grandest night of the ball season, held on the transformed State Opera stage.

events.name: Wiener Festwochen
events.note: The city's leading festival of theatre, opera, dance and music.

events.name: Christmas markets
events.note: Squares from Rathausplatz to Schönbrunn fill with stalls and Punsch.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in the First District near the Hotel Sacher or Bristol for opera, palaces and the great coffee houses at your door; dress is more formal here than elsewhere, jacket for dinner and the opera, and book State Opera or Musikverein tickets ahead.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Vienna International Airport (VIE) is a smooth 20-minute run from the centre, where a chauffeured car meets you and delivers you to the Ringstrasse hotels.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: The imperial centre is elegantly walkable; a private car covers the rest, and the fiaker (horse carriage) is a charming, unhurried way to see the old city.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Comprehensive; an eSIM works instantly and wifi is fast across the city.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Euros (EUR); cards are widely accepted though some traditional coffee houses still prefer cash, so carry a little, and tipping runs around 5–10 percent.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May to September is warm and gracious for the palaces and gardens; December has the celebrated Christmas markets and ball season. January and February are cold and often grey, and August can be crowded and hot.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi on Austrian Airlines and Air India, about 8h20; from Mumbai and Bengaluru usually one stop via Vienna or a Gulf hub. Austrian business is the natural pick, and Vienna airport is compact with a quick 16-minute City Airport Train into the centre.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required beyond routine; Vienna is consistently rated among the world's safest and most liveable cities. Tap water comes straight from Alpine springs and is famously clean.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian and Jain travellers are well served. Restaurant Bombay in the 7th district explicitly offers Jain food, and the city has a strong spread of Indian and vegetarian kitchens across the centre.
